prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics and physics.
Ability to solve differential equations and apply Fourier and Laplace transforms.
Understanding of fundamental electrical engineering concepts.
Knowledge of basic control theory (Bode diagrams, feedback systems).

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the fundamental knowledge required for the analysis of basic electronic circuits, both analog and digital, which can be integrated into automation systems.
Prepare students for potential career opportunities in companies involved in the design/production of electromedical instruments, where electronics plays a significant role.

Acquire both theoretical and practical knowledge of basic electronic circuits, analog and digital, with the goal of being able to design and build potential prototypes/demonstrators and use innovative instrumentation in the medical field.
Appropriately design analog and digital circuits, with particular focus on their integration into automation systems, especially in medical applications.
Analyze a circuit, sizing it appropriately for the final application, and validating its performance by comparing it with the project requirements.
Describe a solution to a specific problem with an adequate level of formalism and appropriate language, collaborating effectively within a workgroup.

Given a problem, reflect on the knowledge and skills acquired during their studies, evaluate different solution strategies, and choose the most suitable one for specific circumstances, being aware of the limitations and strengths of the chosen approach.

syllabus_topics: Operational Amplifiers Ideal operational amplifier: definition, characteristics, inverting and non-inverting configurations
Numerical and experimental exercises with operational amplifier circuits
Voltage-current characteristic: forward bias region, reverse bias region, breakdown region
Models of the diode’s forward characteristic
Rectifier circuits: half-wave rectifier, full-wave rectifier, bridge rectifier, precision half-wave rectifier (super diode)
Experimental exercises with diode and LED circuits
Digital Circuits Introduction to digital electronics
Logic inverter as the fundamental binary element
Transfer characteristic of a logic inverter
Integrated Circuit Technologies Moore’s Law: integration scales of integrated circuits
Silicon as the primary material in electronic and optical devices
Fabrication processes of the P-N junction
Oxidation, deposition (CVD, PVD - Electron beam), lithography and photolithography
MOS Transistor Structure of the MOS transistor
NMOS Logic Gates NMOS inverter with resistive load
Advanced Logic Circuits Input/output interconnection circuits
Internet of Things (IoT) Platforms Introduction to the Internet of Things
Basic components of an IoT system: sensors, data processing boards, network, actuators
Basic concepts of transducers, sensors, and actuators
Most common data processing electronic boards
Experimental exercise on building an IoT station for heart rate monitoring
teaching_methods: Experimental classroom exercise focused on the analysis of amplifier circuits based on Operational Amplifiers
Experimental classroom exercise focused on the analysis of circuits with diodes and LED diodes
Experimental classroom exercise focused on the analysis of an IoT station for monitoring medical parameters
assessment_rules: The final grade will be expressed on a scale of thirty, with honors ("cum laude") awarded in cases where the oral exam fully meets the evaluation criteria. The oral exam will assess the student's knowledge of the topics, their ability to apply them, their critical thinking in analyzing electronic circuits, and the clarity of their explanations. The assessment will consider: a) the level of understanding of the course content, b) the quality of the oral presentation, c) the critical thinking applied to the topics, d) the degree of independent judgment, e) the command of scientific language. The oral exam may include a discussion of topics related to the classroom exercises.
